newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog markets early Friday were steady to up $1.00 per cwt, with prices again underpinned by frigid weather, livestock dealers said.
However, forecasters have said temperatures should moderate somewhat over the weekend and into early next week.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota buyers said hog prices were steady to up $0.50 there at $53.00 to $54.00 in the country and $54.00 to $55.00 at plants. Movement was slowly increasing as winds died down and country roads became passable, they said.
Illinois prices were steady at $53.00 to $54.50 in the country and $55.50 to $56.00 at plants.
Illinois buyers said hog movement should increase as the day progresses and temperatures moderate.
Indiana and Ohio buyers said they were still feeling wind chills of -30 to -50 F and strong winds and drifting snow was still creating havoc with transportation.

No hog movement was reported in central Indiana or central Ohio. However, if conditions improve, the buyers said they expected prices $0.50 higher at $51.50 to $52.00 in the country and $53.00 to $54.00 at plants.
